title: Brucie: From Reluctant Recruit to the Team Everyone Is Chasing
body: Ramon wasn't even sure he wanted in when the Buckaroo Football League launched in 2023, and his first season with Araleasers played like a man still deciding. He went 4-10, scored 1,375.3 points, and limped in as the 6 seed, making exactly zero trades and two pickups all year. Only Sonny's Ben Dover kept him from the basement, and Brucie took a 5th-place finish as his welcome to the league.

Then 2024 happened. Same roster-building philosophy (zero trades, one pickup), much better results: a 7-7 record, the 3 seed, and a playoff win that carried Araleasers all the way to Buckaroo Bowl II. Kaushal's Habibsters ended the dream there, which fits a grudge that runs deep: Habib owns a 8-4 edge over Ramon all-time and handed him his career-worst 56.4 in week 12 that season. Still, a runner-up finish from a guy who almost didn't sign up is a heck of a second act.

2025 is the chapter the league will never let go. Araleasers scored a career-high 1,523.7 points across the season, but Ramon was booted for inactivity after week 8, and the renamed Ramon's Remains played on without him, opening with a 94.76-92.02 win over Philly. The ghost ship logged four trades and eight pickups, finished 5-11 as the 5 seed and landed 5th, and every one of those results sits on Brucie's record with an asterisk. Somewhere in there is a lesson about how much the team needed its manager, and nobody can agree which way it points.

Now he's back, and it's not funny anymore, at least not for the other seven. No Banner only HULK opened 2026 by dropping a career-best 177.9 on Kai in week 1, sits at 6-1 with 927.4 points, and carries 36% title odds into the stretch, with one trade and four pickups showing a manager who's actually pushing buttons. Being the guy the league loves rooting against has never looked more like being the guy the league can't beat.

The head-to-head ledger tells the rest. Ramon has Mekhi's number at 6-3 and is a perfect 1-0 against both newcomers, Zoe and JMoney, while the old guard still holds the upper hand: Sonny leads 7-5, Randy 7-4, and Alan 6-5. A Chicago-born Bills fan with no Buckaroo Bowl rings and no last-place finishes, Brucie has never been the champ or the punchline in the standings. If this season holds, that first column is about to change.
